lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The dates leave an unexplained 10-month gap between the B.S. and the first listed role.
The 35% accuracy increase lacks a metric, evaluation set and comparison.
The reviewer-disagreement rate does not define how disagreement was counted.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the percentages are based on cases, signals or another unit.

items.says: The routing description is cumbersome to parse.
The method details come before the call and latency reductions.
Assistant-only loss masking does not by itself teach the model to reproduce tool outputs faithfully.
items.because: It selects tokens for training loss; tool outputs are not directly supervised unless included in the assistant targets.

items.says: The bullet repeats the adapter fine-tuning method already stated with the accuracy result.
items.because: It takes space without establishing a distinct contribution or result.

items.says: The description does not explain how the extracted features support triage.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the system did with the features to support inspection.

items.says: The backlog reduction needs “by” before “68%.”
items.because: Without it, the phrase does not clearly state the amount of the reduction.

items.says: The strongest achievement in this entry is not the opening bullet.
Switching from FP32 to BF16 alone does not establish a 4× reduction in total fine-tuning GPU memory.
items.because: Total memory also includes activations, gradients and optimizer state, so the overall reduction varies.

items.says: The long fine-tuning modifier slows the reader before the result.
The load-test result is buried in a long trailing clause.
The bullet shifts tense and describes ongoing maintenance instead of a specific action.
items.because: “Adds” conflicts with the ended role’s past-tense framing, while “Maintained” emphasizes a continuing responsibility.

items.says: The three-day release-cycle duration lacks a comparison and a definition.
The backlog and dispatch-delay result has no measure.
items.because: Without a before-and-after measure, the reader cannot judge the operational benefit’s scale.

items.says: The migration result is not the opening achievement in this entry.
“AI-first engineering practices” does not identify the practice introduced.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the project owner built or changed.

items.says: The claimed delivery and downstream benefits are vague and unsupported by a specific result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what changed or how the work helped downstream teams.

items.says: “Budgeted context layers” is specialist shorthand that may not be clear outside the team.
The concurrency and cache-write result is not the opening achievement in this entry.
“50-way fan-out” is specialist shorthand that may slow unfamiliar readers.
The metrics contribution names broad categories but no representative metric or resulting capability.
The 0.89 Kendall correlation does not identify the two quantities being compared.
items.because: Without them, a reader cannot interpret what the coefficient demonstrates about the evaluator.

items.says: The degradation-trial result is not the opening achievement in this entry.
The line does not explain what the screening determines.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how the signals and features guide a triage decision.

items.says: “Triage branch” is jargon.
items.because: The technical contribution is difficult to picture.

items.says: The sensor-triage claim repeats the Mobility Systems backlog achievement and is unrelated to this project.
items.because: The same backlog reduction and signal count appear in both entries, leaving unclear where the work belongs or whether it is credited twice.
